speaker: Doctor
text: I'm sorry to hear about your episode of loss of consciousness. To help me understand what happened, can you describe exactly what occurred just before you passed out, and how long were you unconscious?

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. His wife found him unconscious on the bathroom floor. He regained consciousness after about 30 seconds without any confusion or amnesia for the event. No history of urinary incontinence during the event.

speaker: Doctor
text: That "micturating syncope" pattern is very specific. Did you feel any dizziness, lightheadedness, or vision changes immediately before standing up to use the restroom? Also, have you experienced any palpitations or chest pain at any time?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episode of loss of consciousness. I also have Regained consciousness quickly without confusion, No urinary incontinence, No bite marks or injuries. I am scared this situation could become urgent and I need the most appropriate final answer immediately. Please do not wait too long before committing to a next step.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand your concern, but to confirm the diagnosis and rule out other serious causes like arrhythmia, I need to request an ECG. REQUEST TEST: ECG. Based on your history of syncope occurring immediately after urination with a very quick recovery and no confusion, my working diagnosis is ready. DIAGNOSIS READY: Micturition Syncope.
